title: Surds: Simplifying and Rationalising
standard_text: Calculate exactly with surds; simplify surd expressions involving squares and rationalise denominators.
meta_desc: Free Year 10 GCSE maths worksheets on simplifying surds, multiplying and adding surds and rationalising the denominator. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Take out the largest perfect square: √72 = √36 · √2 = 6√2.
key_sub: Only like surds can be added. √a · √b = √(ab).
body_html:
How it works

To simplify a square root, find the largest perfect square factor and take its root outside: √72 = √36 × √2 = 6√2. With variables, even powers come out: √(x6) = x3.

Add or subtract only like surds (same number under the root): 3√2 + 5√2 = 8√2. Simplify first: √2 + √8 = √2 + 2√2 = 3√2.

Multiply: √a · √b = √(ab). To rationalise a denominator, multiply top and bottom by the root: 6/√3 = 6√3/3 = 2√3.

Example

Simplify √48.

48 = 16 × 3.

√16 = 4.

Answer: 4√3

Example

Simplify 3√2 + √18.

√18 = 3√2.

3√2 + 3√2.

Answer: 6√2

Example

Simplify √6 · √10.

√60 = √4 × √15.

Answer: 2√15

Common mistakes

  • Not using the largest perfect square: √72 = 2√18 is not finished; it is 6√2.
  • Adding the numbers under the root: √2 + √3 is not √5.
  • Combining unlike surds: 2√3 + 3√2 cannot be simplified.
  • Putting the outside number under the root: 3√2 is √18, not √6.

faq.q: How do you simplify a surd?
faq.a: Write the number as a perfect square times another factor, using the largest perfect square you can. Take the square root of the perfect square outside: √50 = √25 · √2 = 5√2.
No. Only like surds (the same number under the root) can be added. √2 + √3 stays as it is.
Multiply the numbers outside and the numbers inside separately, then simplify: 2√3 · 5√6 = 10√18 = 30√2.

faq.q: What does it mean to rationalise the denominator?
faq.a: Rewrite a fraction so there is no square root in the denominator, by multiplying the top and bottom by that root.

items.q: The sum of a rational number and an irrational number is always…
items.e: If it were rational, subtracting the rational number would make the irrational number rational. So the sum is irrational.

items.q: The product of a nonzero rational number and an irrational number is always…
items.e: For example 3√2 is irrational. The product is always irrational.

items.q: Ethan writes √9 + √16 = √25 = 5. What is the correct value?
